correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined two-qubit GKLS generator, exponentiating the single-excitation non-Hermitian block gives exact under/critical/overdamped transfer. The reduced density matrix yields pointwise passivity exactly. Under damping, log transfer is strictly concave within each Rabi lobe, and unique peak times give the explicit exponential peak height, where the peak-loss exponent increases strictly from 0 past log2. The exact ceiling counts only strict positive-work intervals; F_k roots are ordered, with the stated large-index asymptotic. Nondegenerate peak curvature equals -2J^2 and supplies the fixed-lobe square-root width and linear peak-work laws. At and beyond critical damping, peak transfer is at most exp(-2), hence passive for the initially inverted charger. A uniform lobe-phase squeeze under weak damping and Riemann summation gives the Catalan total-duration limit. Direct full 16-dimensional GKLS matrix-exponential and all-threshold checker replay passed 4348 bounded tests; these are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The observable is the actual count and total temporal measure of strictly positive locally extractable work during an exchange charging operation, not an arbitrarily selected finite invariant. The exact damping staircase shows that operational nonpassivity ends at the loss-to-coupling ratio about 1.0211, well before the exceptional-point transition the loss-to-coupling ratio=4. The sharp square-root shrinking of each surviving extraction window quantifies switching-time sensitivity, and the universal Catalan constant determines the entire weak-loss active-time budget. The coherent-versus-incoherent charger distinction identifies a singular physical boundary. These are motivated global quantities not captured by a single-time ergotropy plot. They make no claim of finite experimental detection threshold or complete-cycle charging efficiency.
